newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss test battle readiness with air raid sirens.
newsitem.headline: Swiss test battle readiness with air raid sirens.

text.p: Switzerland's trademark tinkling cow bells will be drowned out by a nationwide cacophony of air raid sirens on Wednesday as this peaceful Alpine haven tests its readiness for war or invasion that will most likely never come.
Civil defence officials said that thousands of sirens and alarms across Switzerland would ring several times from 1230 GMT Wednesday as part of a once-yearly test.

"Stay in your homes or in your office, listen to the national radio, close your doors and windows," said a sign put up at the weekend on the shores of Lake Leman in tranquil Geneva, reminding residents of their civil defence duties.
In Geneva, 89 air raid sirens and alarms will ring for several minutes, said Andre Ollier, an official of the city's Federal Office of Civil Defence.

The sirens in Geneva were installed in the 1940s but have never been used to signal an emergency, Ollier said. Citizens should know to listen to the radio for instructions in the event of a disaster, he added.

Switzerland has one of the world's most extensive civil defence systems including a network of nuclear shelters in homes and buildings designated as shelters. By law, they must be stocked with medical and survival supplies -- although many residents use the shelter to store their wine.
"We've never had problems or war here," said Ollier. "But it's important that we're always ready."
But ready for what? The Swiss, secure in their mountains and surrounded on all sides by the European Union, have rarely experienced war.
They have not fought a battle since a French army under Francois I beat them in 1515 at Marignano, in what is now Italy.
They have an army which can turn out 400,000 soldiers within days, with almost all able-bodied men keeping their guns and ammunition in their cupboards at home. But they lack enemies.
